articles.title: Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ for International Features Race
articles.summary: “La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award. Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved, ”starring Javier Bardem, and Alauda Ruix de Azua’s Goya and San Sebastián winner “Sundays” also figured in…
body: “ La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi ’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award.
Any other Oscar entry choice from Spain than “La Bola Negra,” announced Wednesday by Alejandro Amenábar on behalf of Spain’s Academia de Cine, would have been a huge shock.
The choice came after a second-round vote by Academy members, following the Sept. 3 selection of “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sundays” as the country’s three shortlisted titles.

World premiering in Cannes main competition, “La Bola Negra” first caught attention by scoring a 16 minute standing ovation at its world premiere on the Croisette. It caused a further splash winning best director, shared with Paweł Pawlikowski for “Fatherland.”
points: “La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s submission for the 2027 international feature film Academy Award.

articles.title: ‘Vivant’ Tops Asia Streaming Chart, First Japanese Drama to Lead, Report Finds
articles.summary: TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market.
body: The finding comes from a new ampd Vision report titled “Vivant: A TV Broadcast Hit, Streamed.”

Beyond the streaming platforms, “Vivant” built a substantial following on YouTube, where related content drew 13.2 million viewers, nearly matching its VOD reach. That audience was spread across more than 1,600 videos posted by 450 channels, totaling 8.8 million hours watched at an average of almost 40 minutes per viewer. A companion show TBS produced alongside the drama, “Villains’ Meeting Room,” averaged more than 1.3 million viewers an episode.

The drama’s success did not extend much beyond Japan’s borders. Some 97% of all “Vivant” viewing came from local audiences, ampd found, a pattern consistent with Japanese dramas’ broader struggles abroad: they land in Netflix’s global top 10 outside Japan just 0.3 times a month on average, well behind Korean dramas at 4.1 times and Japanese anime at 1.4.

articles.title: The Cycle of Love review – a 6,000-mile bike ride caps a real life Swedish-Indian romance
articles.summary: One Oscar-winning director, one horoscope-prompted meet-cute and a continent-crossing cyclist – is this the start of documentaries that make you happy-cry? Here is a story that on the face of it seems so wildly unlikely it can only be true.
body: As we hear the now elderly young lovers describe what they were thinking at the time, we watch Lobo and Dale act out the journey, with poor PK getting into a few scrapes that set him back a few steps as he plods his way westward. Some of the most touching interludes are the interactions he has with strangers along the way that seem incredibly naturalistic and semi-improvised. Cynics might quibble that one can’t help wondering what darker parts of the story have been left out, and note that the actors chosen to play the lovers are a few notches more conventionally beautiful than the actual people – but every love story has its soft focus, flaw-concealing fudges so we’ll let it slide here.

articles.title: Peter Jackson’s Weta FX to Talk AI as Netflix’s Creative Asia Spotlights ‘Possible Love’ in Busan
articles.summary: Netflix and the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) are bringing back Creative Asia for a third consecutive year, with the program set for Oct. 10 at Dongseo University’s Centum Campus.
body: BIFF, the Asian Film Commissions Network (AFCNet) and the Motion Picture Association (MPA) all helped shape this year’s lineup.

Cinematographer Kim Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on shaping the visual world of Venice winner “ Possible Love,” walking through the choices he made with director Lee Chang-dong, including trading artificial lighting setups for natural light, with scenes from the film used to illustrate his points. The film is playing at BIFF.

The masterclass slate opens with “Location and Storytelling,” moderated by Busan Asian Film School professor James Bang, with input from Lauren Cooper of the Location Managers Guild International, “Perfect Days” producer Reiko Kunieda and Sung Q Lee. Director Han Jun-hee, known for “D.P. 1 & 2,” “Weak Hero Class 1 & 2” and “The Blue Road,” follows with a session on shaping unexpected material into resonant stories.

articles.title: All support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour quit after Macklemore dropped
articles.summary: The star said he was not responsible for Macklemore being dropped from the line-up after he made pro-Palestinian statements on stage.
body: All of the remaining support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour have quit, after the rapper Macklemore was dropped from the line-up for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage.
Among them were Finneas, the brother of pop star Billie Eilish, who said in a statement: "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed."
Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish band Lukas Graham also announced their departure. Irish folk band Beoga, who perform with Sheeran on stage every night, dropped out too.
The announcements came hours after Sheeran said he would not be drawn into a public debate over Gaza, and stressed he was not responsible for Macklemore being removed from the tour.
points: The star said he was not responsible for Macklemore being dropped from the line-up after he made pro-Palestinian statements on stage.

articles.title: ‘Pride and Prejudice’ Premiere Date Set at Netflix, Full Cast Photos Unveiled
articles.summary: It is totally the year of yearning — here's a look at Emma Corrin, Jack Lowden, Rufus Sewell, Louis Partridge, Daryl McCormack and Freya Mavor in the six-part adaptation of Austen's beloved novel.
body: Bonnets at the ready: The six-part Pride and Prejudice is coming to Netflix Dec. 3.

Series writer Dolly Alderton ( Everything I Know About Love, Ghosts ) gave the Jane Austen Festival in Bath, England the first full look at every single cast member, including Olivia Colman as Mrs. Bennet, Rufus Sewell as Mr. Bennet and Louis Partridge as the roguish Mr. Wickham.

In a year rife with regency drama for loyal fans — the world premiere of Focus Features’ Sense and Sensibility took place just last night, where THR caught up with stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and George MacKay — the series will “join the yearn-aissance in the autumn to faithfully bring Jane Austen’s iconic story back to life for audiences that cherish it, whilst inspiring a new generation to fall in love with it for the first time,” said Netflix.

The streaming platform also confirmed on Wednesday that the six episodes “will hew closely to the 1813 novel — which has captivated readers for centuries with its ever-relevant social commentary, razor-sharp wit, and indelible love story — but also take some thoughtful creative turns.”

articles.title: ‘This should be condemned by any thinking human’: film industry rallies behind NAZA directors
articles.summary: Backing comes after Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor were threatened with having their citizenship revoked and accused of treason. Film industry heavyweights across the globe have expressed solidarity with Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of documentary NAZA, who have…
body: NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym euphemistically used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. It includes interviews with 24 Israeli military or intelligence soldiers and officers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza, resulting in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.
The film builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and the Guardian between 2023 and 2025.

The 80-minute documentary won the special jury prize at this year’s Venice film festival on Saturday, after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. On Sunday, Israel’s culture minister, Miki Zohar, accused the directors of being willing to “harm their homeland in order to receive applause from antisemites around the world”.
“I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for treason against the state,” Zohar wrote on X.

articles.title: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Trailer: Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon Face Royal Betrayal in Disney+’s Lavish K-Drama
articles.summary: Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young co-star in the big-budget adaptation of the Naver Webtoon phenomenon, which has amassed nearly 3 billion views worldwide.
body: “For the first time, I began to wonder — Do I love my husband?”

Shin Min-a stars as Navier, the beloved empress of the fictional Eastern Kingdom, whose seemingly impeccable royal marriage to Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon) begins to unravel when he falls for Rashta (Lee Se-young), a runaway slave newly arrived at court. As romantic loyalties shift and palace ambitions collide, Navier finds herself increasingly drawn toward Crown Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk), heir to the rival Western Kingdom.

When Sovieshu ultimately seeks to cast his wife aside, Navier agrees to his demands on one audacious condition: that she be permitted to remarry Heinrey. The ensuing romantic and political entanglement threatens not only the four characters’ relationships but the balance of power between their kingdoms.
The show is directed by Cho Su-won, whose previous credits include I Can Hear Your Voice, Pinocchio and Still 17, from scripts by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choong-yeol.

articles.title: ‘Neagley’ Review: Amazon’s ‘Reacher’ Spinoff Delivers Similarly Pulpy Pleasures, Despite Filler and Questionable Character Choices
articles.summary: Maria Sten takes the spotlight as a Chicago private investigator looking into a rural cult and occasionally hanging out with Jack Reacher (guest star Alan Ritchson).
body: In Lee Child’s ongoing series of novels focused on outsized American ronin Jack Reacher, Frances Neagley is perhaps the character Reacher trusts the most and — in a franchise whose protagonist wanders the country picking up only a small selection of new allies in each installment — one of the few to recur across 30 books.

Neagley, developed for TV by Santora and Nicholas Wootton (Child was sensible enough to make his primary partner on the book series a woman of color, while Santora… did not make a similar choice), arrives precisely as the fourth Reacher season is wrapping up on Amazon.
The two series are not narratively connected, though Alan Ritchson makes multiple Neagley appearances so that Reacher can give Neagley his blessing to have her own onscreen existence.

articles.title: Trump says Kennedy Center to close as court rules his name must stay off building
articles.summary: The Trump-appointed board was blocked from adding the inscription "Renovated and Restored by President Donald J. Trump".
body: The Kennedy Center board has voted to close the performing arts centre for two years, just as a US judge blocked it from adding President Donald Trump's name back to the building.
In May, the same judge ordered the removal of Trump's name and blocked its temporary closure for proposed renovations.
Trump announced the addition of his name to the institution, among other rebranding measures across the nation's capital, last year.
The judge's written order came less than an hour before the centre's board voted on the closure.
